## Before submitting

- [ ] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

C++ frontend API or graph construction (plus the Python binding defaults)

## Summary

- **`layernorm`: `scale` and `bias` are now optional** in C++ (`nullptr`) and Python (`None`, now the default).
  - Scale without bias (`nn.LayerNorm(bias=False)`) works for any shape. The training `mean`/`inv_variance` dims are unchanged: `input`'s dims, with 1 wherever `scale` is not 1.
  - Bias without scale is refused at `validate()` with `INVALID_VALUE`. The backend rejects it (`hasBiasDesc() && !hasScaleDesc()`, `CUDNN_STATUS_BAD_PARAM`), and the FE error now says to pass a scale of ones.
  - With neither, the same rule as RMSNorm without a scale (#1542) applies: `input` may have at most one non-unit dimension after the first, or, in training, the caller sets the stats dims. Otherwise the node refuses, because the backend's inference default (normalize H only for `{B,S,H}`) and the inferred training stats `{B,1,1}` (normalize S×H) disagree.
- **`adalayernorm`: `bias` is now optional.** Its Python binding has always defaulted `bias` to `None`. `scale` stays required.
- `Graph::layernorm` / `Graph::adalayernorm` keep `nullptr` out of the inputs map, as `Graph::rmsnorm` does since #1542.
- `docs/operations/Normalizations.md` documents the contract.

## Why

On develop, both cases crash in `validate()`: `infer_properties_node` dereferences the null bias.

| Case on develop | Result |
|---|---|
| `layernorm(x, scale, nullptr)` | core dump (`evidence: run927_base.log`, the first no-bias case) |
| `adalayernorm(x, scale, nullptr)`, i.e. the Python default | core dump |
| either one on this branch | validates and runs |

`nn.LayerNorm(bias=False)` is the common case this unblocks.

## Related issues

Part of #188, following #1542 (RMSNorm). The norm backwards still require a scale, so #188 stays open for those.

## API and compatibility impact

- **Additive.** `scale` and `bias` gain `None` defaults in the `layernorm` binding; the positional order is unchanged.
- **No change for graphs that pass both.** The only new refusals are for graphs that previously crashed or were rejected by the backend.
- **Backend qualification** (probe matrix over {scale+bias, scale only, bias only, neither} × {`{N,H,1,1}`, `{B,S,H}`} × {inference, training}, with Y checked against a CPU reference):
  - A100, H100 and B200 with cuDNN 9.27;
  - H100 with 9.12, 9.14, 9.18, 9.20 and 9.24.
  - All served cases match the reference; bias-only is the only backend rejection. Older backends were not qualified.

## Testing

| Where | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| C++ tests, cuDNN 9.27 | `tests "[validate]"` (adds "Layernorm forward with optional scale and bias" and "AdaLayernorm forward without bias", host-only) | 9/9 test cases passed |
| C++ samples, cuDNN 9.27 | `samples "[layernorm],[adalayernorm],[rmsnorm]"` | B200: 21/21; H100, A100: 17 passed / 4 skipped |
| Python, new tests | `pytest norm/graph/test_layernorm.py -k "without or refuses"`: no-bias vs a reference (bf16/fp32), no affine, both refusals, adalayernorm without bias | 12 passed on each of B200, H100, A100 |
| Python, B200 | `pytest -m "L0 or L1 or L2 or L3 or L4" -n 6 norm/graph` | 5189 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed |

After a final behavior-preserving simplification of the stats-dims rule, the extension was rebuilt and `test_layernorm.py` + `test_rmsnorm.py` were rerun: 53 passed on B200; 49 passed and 4 skipped on each of H100 and A100.

+        torch.testing.assert_close(outputs.mean, mean_expected, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-5)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(outputs.inv_variance, inv_variance_expected, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-5)
+
+
+def _layernorm_graph(cudnn_handle, x, *, scale_shape=None, bias_shape=None, phase=cudnn.norm_forward_phase.TRAINING, ada=False):
+    graph = cudnn.pygraph(intermediate_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT, compute_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT, handle=cudnn_handle)
+    X = graph.tensor(name="X", dim=list(x.shape), stride=list(x.stride()), data_type=x.dtype)
+
+    def param(name, shape):
+        return None if shape is None else graph.tensor(name=name, dim=list(shape), stride=list(torch.empty(shape).stride()), data_type=x.dtype)
+
+    S, Bt = param("scale", scale_shape), param("bias", bias_shape)
+    eps = graph.tensor(name="eps", dim=[1] * x.dim(), stride=[1] * x.dim(), is_pass_by_value=True, data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT)
+    norm = graph.adalayernorm if ada else graph.layernorm
+    Y, mean, inv_var = norm(norm_forward_phase=phase, input=X, scale=S, bias=Bt, epsilon=eps)
+    Y.set_output(True).set_data_type(x.dtype)
+    for t in (mean, inv_var):
+        if t is not None:
+            t.set_output(True).set_data_type(cudnn.data_type.FLOAT)
+    return graph, X, S, eps, Y, mean, inv_var
+
+
+def _execute(graph, cudnn_handle, x, variant_pack, stats):
+    graph.validate()
+    graph.build_operation_graph()
+    graph.create_execution_plans([cudnn.heur_mode.A, cudnn.heur_mode.FALLBACK])
+    graph.check_support()
+    graph.build_plans()
+    cudnn.set_stream(handle=cudnn_handle, stream=torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream)
+    out = {t: torch.full([int(d) for d in t.get_dim()], float("nan"), device="cuda") for t in stats if t is not None}
+    workspace = torch.empty(graph.get_workspace_size(), device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8)
+    graph.execute({**variant_pack, **out}, workspace, handle=cudnn_handle)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return out
